final_report.summary: Built a complete Intelligent Subprocess Gate system that replaces AtlasForge's simple binary CPU-threshold check with a multi-signal subprocess classifier, adaptive EMA-learned timeouts, GPU-correlated training detection, and stall monitoring. Cycle 1 delivered the full core library with 135 passing tests across 7 modules. Cycle 2 hardened the system with thread safety, integrated it into the live AtlasForge context watcher and dashboard, converted tests to standard pytest, created a profile database seeding script, added real GPU training detection verification on RTX 3070, and expanded the test suite to 165 passing tests. The system is production-ready and wired end-to-end.
key_achievements: Multi-signal subprocess classifier with 5 process types (TRAINING, COMPILATION, DATA_PROCESSING, TESTING, GENERAL) using GPU correlation (0.95 confidence), command-line keyword matching (0.85), and resource heuristics (0.5-0.7)
SQLite-backed EMA learning system that adapts timeouts based on historical execution durations with outlier rejection at 3-sigma
Stall detection via sliding-window progress monitoring with per-process-type confirmation thresholds (Training=6, Compilation=4, etc.)
NVIDIA GPU integration via pynvml with graceful degradation when no GPU present
Live integration into AtlasForge context_watcher.py replacing _has_active_children() with rich GateDecision logging
Dashboard widget at /api/subprocess-gate/status with WebSocket room for real-time updates
Thread-safe ProgressMonitor with explicit locks (safe for non-CPython runtimes)
Real GPU training detection verified on RTX 3070 with confidence=1.000
Profile database bootstrap script for instant adaptive behavior (bypasses 10-sample cold start)
165/165 tests passing (60 integration + 76 adversarial + 29 cycle-2 adversarial)
challenges_overcome: Designed vote-resolution algorithm for conflicting classification signals (GPU says TRAINING, keywords say COMPILATION) using confidence-weighted summation
Cold-start problem for EMA learning solved with synthetic seeding script that generates 10 Gaussian-distributed samples per process type
Thread safety for ProgressMonitor's shared tracker dictionary required careful lock placement around all mutation and read operations
GPU adapter needed graceful degradation path for systems without NVIDIA GPUs while still providing full functionality when available
Stall detection required different sensitivity thresholds per process type since training runs have naturally longer quiet periods than compilations
lessons_learned: Multi-signal classification with weighted vote resolution is more robust than single-threshold decisions - the confidence-weighted approach naturally handles conflicting signals
EMA-based adaptive timeouts need careful cold-start handling; pre-seeding with synthetic data from base timeouts provides immediate benefit without waiting for real samples
Fail-open design (returning allow-handoff on exception) is critical for infrastructure gates - a crash in the gate should never block the parent system
Real GPU testing on actual hardware catches issues that mocked tests miss entirely - NVML process correlation timing is non-trivial

Modular monolith architecture with clean dependency direction (adapters -> core, orchestration -> core + adapters) made Cycle 2 integration straightforward since each module could be hardened independently
